body.back: Books in which transactions are first recorded from source documents, before being posted to the ledger accounts.
body.front: What are books of original entry?
body.hint: Original = first place a transaction is written down.

body.back: Sales journal, purchases journal, sales returns journal, purchases returns journal, cash book, general journal.
body.front: Name the six books of original entry commonly used in IGCSE Accounting.
body.hint: Think: sales, purchases, their returns, cash, general.

body.back: Credit sales of goods that the business normally sells, taken from sales invoices.
body.front: What is recorded in the sales journal?
body.hint: Credit + goods for resale + sales invoice.

body.back: Credit purchases of goods for resale, taken from purchase invoices received from suppliers.
body.front: What is recorded in the purchases journal?
body.hint: Only goods for resale, not assets.

body.back: Goods returned to the business by credit customers, taken from credit notes issued.
body.front: What is recorded in the sales returns journal?
body.hint: Returns inwards = customers send goods back.

body.back: Goods returned by the business to suppliers, taken from credit notes received.
body.front: What is recorded in the purchases returns journal?
body.hint: Returns outwards = we send goods back.

body.back: Sales invoice (a copy of the invoice sent to the customer).
body.front: What is the source document for the sales journal?
body.hint: We issue it, so we keep a copy.

body.back: Purchase invoice received from the supplier.
body.front: What is the source document for the purchases journal?
body.hint: Supplier issues it, we receive it.

body.back: Credit note issued by the business to the customer.
body.front: What is the source document for the sales returns journal?

body.back: Credit note received from the supplier.
body.front: What is the source document for the purchases returns journal?

body.back: A book of original entry and part of the ledger, recording receipts and payments of cash and bank transactions.
Recording transactions not recorded in other journals, such as purchase of non-current assets on credit, opening entries, correction of errors.
body.front: What is the general journal used for?

body.back: Date, accounts to be debited and credited, amounts, and a narrative explaining the transaction.
body.front: What details are shown for each entry in the general journal?

body.back: They reduce the volume of entries in the ledger, provide a record of transactions, and help locate errors.
body.front: Why are books of original entry used?

body.back: No. They only list transactions; double entry is completed when totals and entries are posted to the ledger accounts.
